answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. What this achieves is a system where the cost of an attack is public and provable, so the whole network can trust verdicts without trusting any single identity. Consider a pulse as the anchor of the cost. A cedar stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a ocean...
